newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Gilts to fall to 113-24 if 114-02 fails.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Gilts to fall to 113-24 if 114-02 fails.

text.p: September gilt futures traded on LIFFE will pull back on Friday to support from old lows around 113-24 if congestion around 114-02/05 gives way, technical analysts said.
Traders said Thursday's quarter-point interest rate rise meant there was little long end demand, particularly as more rate hikes are expected.

"Everyone piled into the long end in the hope that the newly independent Bank of England would get its act together," said Marc Ostwald, technical analyst at London Bond Broking Company. "People are selling on rallies rather than buying on dips."
September long gilts were up 3/32 at 114-10 by 0705 GMT.
Ostwald said the contract may enjoy a short-term rally from the initial congestive support, but that the lure of the the early July lows of 113-24 and 113-25 would prove inexorable.
"Any bounce on the back of good performances elsewhere will hit resistance at 114-14/17, lows set this week," said Ostwald.
Analysts at RBS Futures said Thursday's price action formed an inverted hammer, a potential bottom pattern suggesting the recent sell-off from Monday's 115-02 high has run its course.
"Confirmation is required today, so Sept must build from the start to get the bulls back on track," an RBS note said.
September gilts also face resistance at 114-14, a 38.2 percent retracement of the losses from 115-02 to 114-02, RBS said.
Ostwald said a break above this level would target 114-29, the high set on July 8.
At the short end, December short sterling futures were up two basis points at 92.61 by 0730 GMT. RBS pegged resistance at 92.63, and support at 92.57.
